title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RUSS LEARNS SPANISH
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Russ Ferguson, a bridge painter from Camden, New Jersey.
He hangs off bridges two hundred feet up without blinking.
But one Christmas Eve, a tiny grandmother left him speechless.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE NODDING
segments.quote: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
segments.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
lines: His son Kevin's fiancée, Isabel, invited Russ to her big Puerto Rican family's Christmas Eve.
Thirty relatives, all talking Spanish. Russ just nodded, and got four plates of roast pork.
Driving home, Kevin quoted Ludwig Wittgenstein, an Austrian philosopher:
The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
Russ's world was one nod wide. Next morning, he started Spanish lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: BITTER ROOTS
segments.quote: The roots of education are bitter, but the fruit is sweet.
segments.author: Aristotle
lines: Spanish was hard. His rolled R sounded like a leaf blower that wouldn't start.
He was ready to quit. Then he found a line from Aristotle:
The roots of education are bitter, but the fruit is sweet.
So he kept chewing. Twenty minutes a day, up on the bridge.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NAME
segments.quote: Remember that a person's name is to that person the sweetest and most important sound in any language.
segments.author: Dale Carnegie
lines: Confession: for a year, Russ had said Grandma's name wrong.
She was Doña Carmen Quiñones, and too polite to correct him.
His buddy Hector taped a card from Dale Carnegie to his lunch box:
Remember that a person's name is to that person the sweetest and most important sound in any language.
Russ practiced it until the whole paint crew could say it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BIG MISTAKE
segments.quote: Laughter is the shortest distance between two people.
segments.author: Victor Borge
lines: At Easter, Russ finally tried his Spanish on the whole family.
He meant to say, I'm embarrassed. He actually said, I'm pregnant.
Silence. Then he remembered the comedian Victor Borge:
Laughter is the shortest distance between two people.
So Russ laughed first. Doña Carmen laughed until she cried, then hugged him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: HIS OWN WORDS
segments.quote: He who does not speak foreign languages knows nothing about his own.
segments.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
lines: Then Russ started noticing his own English.
He'd never known what a verb was. He'd just used them for fifty-six years.
Isabel showed him a line from Goethe, the German writer:
He who does not speak foreign languages knows nothing about his own.
So Russ began choosing his words with care, in both languages.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TOAST
segments.quote: The family is one of nature's masterpieces.
segments.author: George Santayana
lines: Next Christmas Eve, Russ stood up, hands shaking worse than on any bridge.
In slow Spanish, he said, Thank you for giving my son a family, and me too.
Kevin raised his glass and quoted the philosopher George Santayana:
The family is one of nature's masterpieces.
Thirty people cheered. This time, Russ understood every word.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Widen your world. Keep chewing. Say the name right. Laugh first. Mind your words. Love your family.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Widen your world. Keep chewing. Say the name right. Laugh first. Mind your words. Love your family.
Me? I once ordered coffee in Italian. I got a haircut.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
